title: Toni Morrison's Beloved
objective: After this level you can explain how Morrison's Beloved turns the history of slavery into a story about memory.
summary: Morrison's Beloved (1987) grew from the 1856 case of Margaret Garner. It changes the history, tells it from the inside, and breaks time into pieces so the past moves back into the house.

cards.headline: The house at 124 Bluestone Road is haunted, and everyone knows it.
cards.body: Toni Morrison's Beloved (1987) opens in Cincinnati in 1873. In Sethe's house, chairs move by themselves, kettles turn over and handprints appear in cake icing. Sethe, who escaped slavery, believes the ghost is her older daughter, who died before she was two. Why would a mother's home be haunted by her own child?

cards.headline: A true case from 1856
cards.body: The seed is history. In 1856 Margaret Garner, an enslaved woman who had escaped to Cincinnati, was about to be forced back to Kentucky under fugitive slave laws. She killed her infant daughter rather than see the child returned to slavery. The law charged her not with murder but with destroying her owner's property. Morrison came across the case in an 1856 newspaper clipping while compiling The Black Book (1974).

cards.headline: Fiction that answers the record
cards.body: Beloved is not a retelling. Morrison changes the ending: Sethe and her daughter Denver finish the novel alive and free, while the real Margaret Garner was recaptured and died in captivity. Morrison said that telling the story through the characters' inner lives puts authority back in the hands of the enslaved, not the slaveholder. The court record treated a child as property; the novel treats every one of its people as a person.

cards.headline: A past that walks in the door
cards.body: Then a mysterious young woman named Beloved appears, the age Sethe's dead daughter would have been, and Sethe takes her in. The book jumps between its present after the Civil War and flashbacks from before Emancipation, the way painful memory surfaces: in pieces, out of order. Its characters work every day at beating back the past. In Beloved, the past doesn't stay buried. It moves in.

learned: Beloved grew from the 1856 Margaret Garner case
Morrison changed the ending and told it from inside
Its broken timeline mirrors painful memory

questions.prompt: Match each name from the true story behind Beloved with what goes with it.
questions.explanation: The real Margaret Garner was recaptured and died in captivity, while Sethe and her daughter Denver finish the novel alive and free. Morrison found the case while compiling The Black Book (1974).

questions.prompt: How does the structure of Beloved mirror the way its characters remember?

options.label: It jumps between the present and the past, in pieces
It tells events strictly in date order
It covers a single day, told hour by hour in real time
It is written as a series of letters

questions.explanation: The novel moves between its present and pre-Emancipation flashbacks, a structure of fractured memory.

questions.prompt: A legend is told as history, whether or not it happened. Beloved works the other way round. How?

options.label: It insists that every event literally happened
It is openly fiction reimagining a real case
It is a sacred story tied to belief
It ends by stating a moral

questions.explanation: A legend presents itself as history; Beloved presents itself as fiction, reimagining the real Garner case and changing its ending.
